# Machine-file fixtures — provenance

**These files were NOT generated by this SDK. Do not regenerate them from .NET code.**

Every `*.machine` file here was produced by calling `tamga-api`'s own
`encode_machine_file` (`src/shared/crypto/machine_file.rs`) — the same function the
production server uses to emit a `.machine` file — with server-generated signing keys.
They are byte-for-byte what a real checkout returns.

`manifest.json` is part of that same drop and is the contract the tests iterate:
`MachineFileFixtureTests` reads it and derives one test case per entry, so a later
fixture drop needs no test edit.

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | fixture filename in this directory |
| `alg` | the `alg` string inside the file's certificate |
| `encrypted` | whether `enc` is AES-256-GCM ciphertext |
| `enc_is_dot_separated` | whether `enc` is `<nonce_b64>.<ciphertext_b64>` |
| `public_key_b64` | the account public key, in the format the server actually hands out |
| `kid` | the `kid` claim inside the signed payload |
| `license_key` | HKDF input keying material (`null` for plain files) |
| `fingerprint` | HKDF `info` — the machine the file was issued for |
| `expired` | whether the signed `exp` claim had already passed at issue time |
| `scheme` | the license's signing scheme, as a `LicenseScheme` member name |

## Why not self-generated

For two years every SDK in the fleet tested its machine-file reader against a file the
same SDK had just written. That reproduced each SDK's own misreading of the wire format
on both sides of the round trip, so CI stayed green while no SDK could open anything the
server actually emitted — the `enc` layout (M2) and the `alg` grammar (M1) were both
wrong fleet-wide. A fixture that this repo produced proves only that this repo is
self-consistent.

If a case is missing from this set, ask for it to be produced from the server's encoder.
Do not add a hand-rolled `.machine` file to this directory.

## Public key formats (they are not uniform)

The `public_key_b64` values are what the server produces, which is **not** one encoding:

- **Ed25519** — raw 32-byte public key.
- **ECDSA P-256** — raw 65-byte SEC1 uncompressed point (`0x04 || X || Y`), from
  `EcdsaKeyPair::public_key().as_ref()`. **Not** SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER.
- **RSA-2048** — PKCS#1 `RSAPublicKey` DER (270 bytes, `30 82 01 0A ...`), from
  aws-lc-rs `PublicKey::as_ref()`, which `license_signing::extract_public_key` uses.
  Note the account resource's own `public_key` attribute is populated from
  `PublicKey::as_der()` instead, which **is** SubjectPublicKeyInfo — so both RSA
  encodings are reachable in the wild and the SDK accepts either.
